title: Correction and Detention Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
10.     MOS 5831, Correction and Detention Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC
I&L

    a. Summary. Correctional Specialists guard and provide 24-hour
supervision of the daily activities of confined personnel at military
correctional facilities (MCFs) to prevent disturbances and escapes.
Correctional Specialists perform routine inspections, process personnel for
confinement and release, transport prisoners, absentees and deserters; manage
prisoner's funds and personal property, observe and report meaningful changes
in prisoner behavior, report conduct investigations on infractions of the
MCFs published regulations, investigate the whereabouts of military deserters
to facilitate their swift return to military control. Corrections Specialist
also provide commanders with the capability to execute regional detention
facilities in theater with immediate oversight and subject matter expertise
on the safe, humane and efficient care of enemy detainees entrusted to their
care. Typical duties and billets include escort, dorm supervisor, master
control supervisor, mess deck supervisor, duty driver, duty brig supervisor,
command investigator, administration chief, programs chief, and operations
chief billets.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must be able to lift and lower 67 lbs.

            (3) Must possess a GT score of 95 or higher.

            (4) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

            (5) Must possess a high degree of maturity and emotional stability.

        (6) Have no record of civil court conviction that resulted in
confinement.

        (7) Must be able to stand for long periods while wearing/carrying up
to a 80 pound uniform and combat equipment.

        (8) Must have no history of mental, nervous, or emotional disorders
(waivers to this requirement will not be granted).

        (9) Must have no convictions by special or general courts-martial, or
felony convictions or misdemeanor convictions of domestic violence from civil
courts. Waivers will not be granted for convictions by special or general
courts-martial or civil courts for crimes of domestic violence as per
reference (bk), the Lautenberg Amendment.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Corrections and Detention Specialist Course
(A16MN43), USAMPS, Ft Leonard Wood, MO.




                                           3-337                        Enclosure (1)
 3136                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (2) Requests for lateral move into MOS 5831 will be accompanied by an
interview and recommendation by an installation's senior corrections officer,
MOS 5804 (not waiverable).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (ac), Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections Training and
Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Correctional Officers and Jailers 33-3012.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Correction and Detention Specialist, 5831.

            (2) Correctional Counselor, 5832.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
